speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my consultation, I am Dr. Agent. As your newborn care is critical, please tell me: Was the pregnancy term, and did you experience any chorioamnionitis, maternal fever, or prolonged rupture of membranes prior to birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Since the mother had no prenatal care, we need to rule out congenital infections like syphilis or toxoplasmosis. Does the infant have any visible skin rash, jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, or microcephaly on physical exam? Also, were there any abnormal findings noted during the initial newborn screening?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Syphilis with secondary syphilis rash (snuffles/mucocutaneous lesions), congenital cataracts (interstitial keratitis), and sensorineural hearing loss.

REQUEST TEST: VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) titer from infant serum, CBC with smear, and Liver Function Tests.
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundoscopic exam to confirm interstitial keratitis and rash distribution.
